title: A Second Decree to Fight Back
overview: With Haman dead but his order to kill the Jews still in force, Esther and Mordecai win a new royal decree that lets the Jews defend themselves.

parts.label: Haman's power passes on (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: A traitor's property went to the crown, so the king gave Haman's estate to Esther, and she put Mordecai in charge of it. The king's signet ring stamped his seal on official orders, so handing it to Mordecai made him the king's top official in Haman's place.

parts.label: Esther pleads again (vv. 3-6)
parts.note: Haman was gone, but his sealed order to wipe out the Jews on a set day still stood. Esther, safe herself, weeps for her people and tactfully blames Haman for the plan rather than the king who approved it.

parts.label: An order that cannot be undone (vv. 7-10)
parts.note: The king says a sealed royal decree cannot be cancelled, so he lets Mordecai write a second one in his name. It is sent in every script and language of the empire by the fastest royal horses.

parts.label: The right to fight back (vv. 11-14)
parts.note: The new law did not erase the old one; it let Jews gather and kill anyone who attacked them on that same day, and take their goods. Its wording mirrors Haman's decree, and scholars disagree whether it also permits killing the attackers' women and children or means protecting the Jews' own families.

parts.label: Fear turns to celebration (vv. 15-17)
parts.note: Mordecai appears in royal blue, white and purple with a gold crown, a public sign of his new rank, and Jews everywhere feast where they had recently fasted. Many others 'became Jews' out of fear, though it is unclear whether this means true conversion or simply siding openly with them.

disagreement: Christians differ over whether the killing this decree allows should be read as rightful self-defense the book approves, or as vengeance the story simply reports without endorsing.
think: When a harmful decision cannot be taken back, is limiting its damage ever enough, and who should bear the cost of doing so?
